description.text: Pudentiana was a Christian virgin and martyr of the second century who is said to have refused to worship the Roman emperors Marcus Aurelius and Antoninus Pius as deities.  She was the eldest daughter of the Roman senator Pudens, and is sometimes locally known as "Potentiana"; she is closely associated with her younger sister Praxedes, who is also regarded as a martyr.

According to her acta and the Martyrology of Reichenau, Pudentiana and Praxedes, together with Pope Pius I, built a baptistry in the church inside their father's house and began baptizing pagans.  She died at the age of sixteen and was buried next to her father in the Priscilla catacombs on the via Salaria.  Although evidence for Pudens exists, there is no direct evidence for Pudentiana or Praxedes, and the early Church may have mistaken their existence.

curiosities.text: Pudentiana’s feast day, 19 May, coincides with the date on which Spanish conquistador Miguel López de Legazpi claimed Manila in 1571; because of this, she was declared patroness of the Philippines and is still mentioned in the Roman Martyrology on that date.
